articleTitle: Research on Virtual LiDAR Wind Measurement Technology for Wind Farms Based on CFD and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: LiDAR data can provide reference for yaw control, load optimization and power curve evaluation of wind turbines. In this study, the virtual LiDAR wind measurement and intelligent prediction technology for wind farm are established based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulation, on-site wind turbine data, LiDAR data, and long short-term memory (LSTM) deep learning model, with the wind farm as the research object. The results show that the established virtual LiDAR wind measurement and short-term intelligent prediction techniques are highly accurate, with the RMSE error less than 1.7279 m/s, and the accuracy is improved by 12.2-29.2% compared with that of the deep learning model based on the measured data, which can provide scientific basis for the virtual LIDAR wind measurement and intelligent prediction of the actual wind farms.

articleTitle: High-Gain DC-DC Converter with Symmetric Interleaved Parallel Structure for Household Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: This paper presents a new symmetric interleaved parallel DC-DC converter topology designed for household photovoltaic systems, offering high output voltage. Compared to conventional DC-DC converters, this topology provides a higher boost gain and a wider range of output voltages. Additionally, the interleaved parallel operation significantly reduces the ripple in the output current and voltage. Moreover, the voltage clamping characteristics of the capacitors in the two power switches within the interleaved array greatly enhance the system's stability and reliability. Finally, a simulation platform has been established to validate the effectiveness of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Research on Transformer Noise and Noise Reduction Measures Based on Multi-physical Field Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: With the ongoing advancements in voltage levels, transformer capacity, and associated parameters, the issue of transformer noise pollution is escalating. It is imperative to promptly implement effective measures for mitigating transformer noise. In this study, a 110kV transformer model is formulated utilizing a finite element simulation platform. Employing an electric-magnetic-force-acoustic multi-physical field coupling method, the stress distribution, flux density distribution, and sound pressure level distribution of the transformer are simulated and analyzed. This investigation elucidates the correlation between transformer noise and excitation voltage frequency. Furthermore, various noise reduction strategies are suggested, encompassing enhancements to the transformer core material and adjustments to the core clamping force, among other methodologies.

articleTitle: Exploring Control Strategies for Flexible Interconnect Devices in High-Ratio Power Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Proposing a flexible interconnection device, based on a back-to-back converter (BTB- VSC), to address issues of unbalanced power distribution and poor power quality arising from numerous power electronic devices connected to the power grid. This solution facilitates power flow regulation between two AC systems, thereby improving the management of power quality. Introducing the topological structure, mathematical model, and control principles of the BTB- VSC, a MATLAB/Simulink simulation verification model is created to validate the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy. The simulation outcomes demonstrate that the related control approach adeptly manages active power transmission and reactive power compensation between the two AC systems. This results in elevated power quality, augmented reliability, and enhanced economic efficiency within the distribution network's operation.

articleTitle: Research on Flow Field Characteristics of SF6 Gas Nozzle
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: The paper introduces how the author built a simulated arc test platform and used a piezoresistive pressure sensor to measure the transient air pressure at two measuring points in the air storage chamber and the nozzle throat under cold flow and arc conditions, and obtained the combustion results. The change process of the gas pressure in the nozzle throat during the arc process was compared with the cold flow results. The test verified the pressurizing effect of the high-temperature arc on the gas in the nozzle throat. The paper also introduces the platform construction, test methods and measurement systems.

articleTitle: High Voltage Fault Current Limiter by Fast Switch with Multiple Breaks in Series
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: As the rapid increase of power grid capacity, the short-circuit current of the grid could be very large in some certain district, which may seriously harm the stability and safe operation of the system. To solve this problem, a fault current limiter with multiple high speed switches in series is proposed in this paper. The features include “one-drag-two” topology and high-potential installation of the electromagnetic repulsion driving mechanism, and isolation transformers are applied to achieve high-potential power supply. Therefore, the insulating pole of the switch can be cancelled, which helps reducing the weight of the moving contact, so that it is easier to realize quick opening and closing. Meanwhile, the problem that the current limiter which is powered by capacitive voltage transformer (CVT) is not able to operate when the system is not charged does not exist in the proposed scheme. In addition, the parameters of the repulsion mechanism are optimized for two coils series connected structure using 3D finite element simulation. Also, the stray capacitances between switches and the ground are extracted, and then the equalizing capacitances are decided to guarantee the uniformity of voltages on each switch. A test system based on LC oscillation is built to test and verify the proposed 220 kV fault current limiter prototype. The dynamic voltage sharing characteristics of the prototype during the transition of the short circuit current to the current limiting reactor are obtained. Furthermore, the opening tests of the prototype with different arcing time are carried out. The test results show that the series-connected fast switches are capable of breaking 40 kA short circuit current with DC component more than 80% in 3ms after receiving the breaking command.

articleTitle: Influence of Train Overvoltage on Grounding Circulation of Traction Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Based on the structure of traction cable, this paper analyzes the mechanism of cable grounding circulation, and discusses the influence of current frequency on grounding circulation. On this basis, the electromagnetic transient simulation software is used to build the traction power supply system, traction cable and EMU VCB operating overvoltage model. The influence of train VCB operating overvoltage on traction cable grounding circulation is simulated and analyzed. The research shows that the VCB operating overvoltage waveform contains high frequency components mainly 800kHz. The effect of the high frequency component on the cable grounding circulation is about 6600 times that of the power frequency current. Finally, the accuracy of the simulation results is verified through the field experiment and the cable grounding circulation test platform.

articleTitle: A New Tightly-Coupled Lidar-Visual-Inertial Odometry with Loop Closures
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Simultaneous Localization And Mapping (SLAM) is a technology aimed at concurrently ascertaining the position of a robot while mapping an unknown environment. Its core involves achieving accurate and stable pose estimation for the robot. Fusion of multiple sensors has been demonstrate to be an effective method for improving accuracy. As the types of information acquired by different sensors increase, it inevitably enhances the robustness of pose estimation. This paper introduces a fusion framework designed for the multi-sensor system that combines lidar, inertial, and visual sensors. It utilizes a factor graph to perform global optimization, so that it enables real-time, high-precision, and stable trajectory prediction and map generation for robots. The system is split into two components: a Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO) subsystem and a Lidar-Inertial Odometry(LIO) subsystem. LIO continuously acquires new point cloud information, extracts features, performs frame-to-frame feature matching for loop closure detection, and append the lidar points into the global map. VIO uses data of the point cloud from LIO for initialization, alternates with LIO processing, and utilizes visual information to apply color rendering to the map. To enhance system robustness, VIO not only directly utilizes point cloud data but also extracts features directly from image information, preventing over-reliance on LIO. Even if one of the subsystems fails, the system can continue to operate. Extensive experiments were conducted on open datasets, demonstrating that our approach achieves more accurate robot pose estimation and produces point cloud maps with color information.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation Method for User Green Attributes Considering Low-carbon Electricity Consumption Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: With the transformation and upgrading of China's energy system, many users offset their carbon emissions by purchasing green electricity and green certificate. Considering the current lack of a comprehensive carbon emission offset mechanism from low-carbon electricity consumption, determining the environmental value of low-carbon electricity and evaluating the green attributes of users are the primary challenges currently faced. To incentivize users to increasingly purchase low-carbon electricity, the theoretical framework for evaluating user's low-carbon electricity consumption is established first based on the carbon flow tracing method and life-cycle theory. Then, based on AHP-entropy method and TOPSIS method, user green attributes evaluation model is construct including four different dimensions of evaluation indicators. Finally, case studies are conducted to analyze green attributes of multiple users considering low-carbon electricity consumption behavior patterns.

articleTitle: Study on the Influence of Traction Reflux on Rail Magnetization in Electrified Railway
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Aiming at the phenomenon of abnormal remanence of rail, a three-dimensional finite element model of locomotive traction circuit is established to simulate the magnetization of rail. The results show that the magnetic field generated by the contact line at the rail and the magnetic field generated by the rail coupling are both less than 0.1Gs when the locomotive is running normally, which is much smaller than the remanent magnetic field of the rail measured in the field of 100Gs, and the influence can be ignored. When the amplitude of locomotive traction current changes, the magnetic field generated on the rail surface can reach 0. 7T, which will retain a certain residual magnetic field and affect the locomotive equipment.

articleTitle: Ensuring Physical Consistency in Power Flow Sample Generation via Automated Tie-Bus Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: With the wide application of data-driven methods in power systems, the requirements for the number and quality of power flow samples are increasingly higher. DC power flow model has the advantages of fast calculation speed and can avoid convergence problems, which has high efficiency in large-scale sample generation. However, the low accuracy and limited calculation scope restrict its further application in sample generation. For instance, the power injection at tie-buses always violates the physical consistency. To this end, this paper aims to study an automated adjustment method to ensure the tie-buses physical consistency of power flow samples. Our proposed method enhances the DC power flow model by integrating an automated tie-bus adjustment algorithm that dynamically corrects power injections to maintain zero injection at tie-buses, thereby adhering to physical laws and improving the realism of power flow simulations. We conduct case studies on the IEEE 118-bus test system to validate the effectiveness of our approach in generating physically consistent power flow samples. The results demonstrate improvements in the tie-bus power injection of the samples compared to other methods, offering a promising solution for power system operators and planners in their quest for high-quality power flow samples.

articleTitle: Low-current Ground Fault Location Method Based on Main Distribution Coordination
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: A low-current grounding fault location method based on the coordination of mains and distribution is proposed, which aims to integrate the main grid-side fault sensing and fault line selection, and the line-side fault location and recovery, so as to quickly realize the small-current grounding fault determination, location and fault recover. It includes the following steps: the first step is to quickly perceive the low-current ground fault bus based on the main network operating data and event alarms; the second step is to perform a trial pull sequence on the faulty bus load outgoing line through the IQ comprehensive method and other sequencing methods and try to pull to determine the fault outgoing line; The third step is to prioritize the line-side distribution network switches for the trial pull scheme; the fourth step is to perform trial pull operations on the line-side switches in sequence according to the line-side switch trial pull sequence in the sequence table, and determine according to the result of the trial pull operation Fault location.

articleTitle: High Interaction Attack Defense Mechanism Based on RASP Technology in Power System Network Security Reinforcement
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: This article explores the high interaction attack defense mechanism based on runtime application self-protection (RASP) technology in power system network security reinforcement. With the rapid development of information technology, network security has become a key factor affecting national security and social stability. This article focuses on a high interaction attack defense mechanism that can monitor the execution process of applications in real-time. This mechanism is good at identifying and mitigating potential attack behaviors, thereby improving the security and reliability of the power system. The experimental results show that the performance of the mechanism has been significantly improved, while reducing the resource consumption rate and false alarm rate to the optimal values of 94.9 points, 10.2%, and 5%, respectively. This study provides innovative solutions for network security protection in the field of power systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic Hysteresis Modelling of Giant Magnetostrictive Actuators Based on NGO-BRNARX
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: To precisely capture the rate-dependent hysteresis observed in giant magnetostrictive actuator, a neural network dynamic model of hysteresis is established based on the extended input space method. A novel dynamic hysteresis operator is formulated to effectively characterize both the trend and dynamic properties inherent to rate-dependent hysteresis, and the extended input space is constructed based on the dynamic hysteresis operator, which can transform the multi-valued mapping of hysteresis into one-to-one mapping, and meanwhile, the dynamic hysteresis operator can be utilised to extract the rate dependence of hysteresis. Construct the neural network NARX (nonlinear autoregressive model with exogenous inputs) model. To enhance the model's predictive accuracy and robustness, the learning rate of the NARX model is optimized via the Northern Eagle algorithm. Additionally, Bayesian regularization techniques are applied to augment the NARX model's generalization capabilities. The efficacy of the proposed model and its estimation algorithm is corroborated by experimental results.

articleTitle: A 110kV Main Transformer Substation Insulation Fault Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: This paper briefly describes the failure situation of qinghe 1 # main transformer, and according to the comprehensive data of high pressure test and oil chromatography test, the failure cause of the A phase winding is analyzed, and finally put forward the reasonable accident prevention measures, to provide reference to prevent the occurrence of similar faults in the future.

articleTitle: Research on the Equilibrium Model of Electrical Energy and Flexible Ramping Market Considering Ramp Capacity Demand Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: As the proportion of renewable energy in the power system increases, the intermittence, variability and uncertainty of its power generation will bring greater operating pressure to the power system, requiring certain flexible adjustment and response capabilities to cope with intermittency. Potential situations such as wind curtailment, light curtailment, and load loss brought about by renewable energy have placed higher requirements on system flexibility. Taking into account the current situation that China's power system flexibility needs to be improved urgently in the context of the new power system, this article first provides an overview of the basic concepts and other aspects of the flexible ramping market mechanism; Secondly, on the basis of considering the calculation of the ramp capacity demand curve, an electricity energy flexible ramping market equilibrium model was constructed to support the decision-making of reasonable capacity allocation among flexible resources in different markets. Finally, simulation was performed on the IEEE 30-bus system to verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design and Application of Intelligent Sensors in Hydropower Station
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: It is particularly critical of the design, development and application of intelligent sensors in hydropower stations under the trend of deep intellectualization and digitalization of hydropower stations. The design and application of intelligent sensors in hydropower stations play an important role in helping the wisdom of hydropower stations, reducing the safety operation and maintenance cost of hydropower station, improving the calculation and analysis ability of hydropower station. In this paper, the relevant technology of intelligent sensors of hydropower station at home and abroad is fully investigated. Then, based on the different data processing characteristics of hydropower station, the communication and data processing solutions of intelligent sensors of hydropower station are proposed. Finally, based on the characteristics of different application scenarios of hydropower stations, three design and development schemes of intelligent sensors for hydropower station are proposed.

articleTitle: Predictive Control Study of Active Anti-rollover Model for Heavy-duty Vehicles Considering Variable Curvature Curves
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Traditional controllers face difficulties in effectively controlling heavy-duty vehicles due to their large mass, high center of gravity, and delayed actuator response. This paper presents an adaptive model predictive control vehicle chassis integrated controller based on a rollover factor model established using the vehicle lateral transfer ratio. The state quantities used in the controller are the yaw rate, the sideslip angle, and the roll angle. The heavy-duty vehicle's anti-rollover performance can be improved by reasonably distributing the additional yaw moment and front steer angle. A virtual real-vehicle test environment and a real online joint simulation were constructed to verify the anti-rollover performance of the vehicle under double land conditions and variable curvature roads while generating additional yaw moment and front steer angle. Additionally, an anti-rollover Hardware-In-Loop test platform was built to ensure the stability and safety of heavy-duty vehicles under variable curvature curves.

articleTitle: A Differentiated ArcGIS-Based Approach for Lightning Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: This paper introduces a differentiated lightning protection method based on ArcGIS platform. The method is optimised for the complex climate and terrain conditions unique to the plateau, and counts thunderstorm days as well as accurately calculates the lightning flash density and lightning trip-out rate by combining grid and the Least Squares methods. The model constructed in ArcGIS is not only capable of handling a large amount of lightning data and importing terrain information, but also capable of adjusting the parameters according to the specific conditions of different regions and presenting the results visually, which ensures the accuracy and universal applicability of the assessment results. In addition, the method provides important technical support for the safe operation of the power system and is a powerful tool for maintenance of distribution networks in plateau areas.

articleTitle: An Adaptive Secondary Frequency Control Strategy for Distributed Energy Resources to Improve the Dynamic Performance of Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Secondary frequency control can converge the frequency to the rated value, which is crucial for stabilizing microgrids (MGs), especially in the islanded mode. Currently, secondary frequency control mainly achieves static operation targets, including accurate frequency recovery and power allocation. Still, dynamic performance is also crucial for the stability of MGs, particularly when synchronous distributed energy resources (DERs) exist in MG systems. Synchronous units will introduce the underdamped oscillation mode, which causes unstable operation of the power grid. Therefore, an adaptive secondary frequency control method is presented for synchronous DERs to enhance islanded MG's frequency dynamics. In the adaptive secondary frequency control scheme, the transient frequency regulation and the steady-state frequency error elimination can be traded off using the system's real-time measurements. Finally, numerical simulation analysis on an IEEE test system operated in the MATLAB/Simulink software validate the superior performance of the adaptive control strategy in enhancing the frequency dynamics of microgrids.

articleTitle: Research on the Detection of False Data Injection Attacks in DC Microgrids Based on Attention Mechanism and DAE-CNN-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Distributed DC microgrid is a typical power information physical system (CPS) that is vulnerable to cyber-attacks. False Data Injection Attack (FDIA) on the information side can change the system's operational state and even destabilize the microgrid system. Most of the existing microgrid cyber attack detection methods in view of linear DC microgrid models. However, there are constant power loads (CPLs) in DC microgrids, which present negative resistive and nonlinear characteristics and are generally nonlinear. For this reason, in this paper, a distributed DC microgrid model with constant power loads is developed and a nonlinear DC microgrid false data injection attack detection method based on the attention mechanism and convolutional bi-directional recurrent neural network is proposed. After adding a known constant power load during the DC microgrid stabilization process, the distributed units suffering from FDIA are identified by comparing the discrepancy between the estimated value of the offline-trained neural network and the actual measured value to distinguish between the load change and the false data injection attack. Finally, a 4-node DC microgrid model is built in MATLAB/Simulink for simulation experiments to validate the effectiveness of the proposed assay.

articleTitle: A Progress Prediction Model Using Res-zLSTM for LOCA in Nuclear Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Predicting the changes in various operation conditions following a loss of coolant accident (LOCA) in a nuclear power plant is of great significance. To enhance the accuracy of prediction, this paper proposes a novel prediction model called Res-zLSTM. The Res-zLSTM model incorporates residual structure and attention mechanisms to effectively mitigate the gradient vanishing problem in traditional Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models. Additionally, it maintains a low network complexity while simultaneously strengthening its ability to learn from long-term sequence data. This allows for accurate predictions of key parameter trends in LOCA conditions. In validation experiments, the Res-zLSTM model was used to predict multiple important operational parameters under different LOCA conditions. The experimental results demonstrate that the Res-zLSTM model exhibits superior prediction accuracy, achieving a maximum improvement of 54% compared to the zLSTM model. While the prediction accuracy of the Res-zLSTM model may be influenced by the changing rate of operation data, its outstanding performance in predicting LOCA conditions provides a novel approach for predicting operation conditions in complex systems.

articleTitle: Aggregated Scheduling Method of Energy Storage and Polycrystalline Silicon Load Based on Production Status
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Considering the constraints of the charging and discharging process of pumped storage devices, as well as the process limitations and production requirements in the production of polycrystalline silicon, a production-state-based aggregated optimization scheduling model is established for pumped storage and polycrystalline silicon enterprises. For the production process of polycrystalline silicon load, the state-task network method is used to establish production process constraints. Taking into account the constraints of the charging and discharging process of pumped storage devices, the objective is to minimize the comprehensive purchasing cost of pumped storage and polycrystalline silicon enterprises. A production-state-based aggregation scheduling for pumped storage and polycrystalline silicon load is constructed, adjusting the charging and discharging status of each unit of pumped storage and the start-stop time of each task of polycrystalline silicon load under the constraint conditions, to ensure equipment safety, normal production, and flexible interaction. Through case simulation, it is verified that the proposed method can guide the participation of pumped storage and polycrystalline silicon aggregation in peak shaving of the power grid as much as possible, while ensuring the safety of pumped storage devices and normal production of polycrystalline silicon enterprises, and enhancing the enthusiasm of polycrystalline silicon load to participate in grid interaction.

articleTitle: A Load Shedding Control Method for Power System Based on Frequency Prediction and Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Modern power systems require fast and effective load shedding to maintain frequency stability, especially during disturbances. Traditional load shedding methods suffer from several short-comings, including slow computational time and negligence of load shedding priorities. To address these challenges, this paper introduces a novel load shedding approach built on frequency prediction and deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Firstly, a dynamic frequency response model of the power system is constructed. This model imitates the dynamic frequency response of the power system through the transfer function, and based on this, the dynamic frequency response indices including the steady-state frequency difference and maximum frequency difference can be calculated. Then, a deep Q network (DQN) based load shedding method is presented through designing DQN parameters including DQN state, action, reward function and training method. Finally, the empirical analysis indicates that the proposed method can achieve a lower frequency nadir and smaller maximum frequency difference than the method based on real-time frequency measurement. Moreover, relative to the model-based method, the proposed method provides faster decision-making speed, contributing positively to system frequency stability.

articleTitle: Gait Learning for 3D Bipedal Robots Based on a Combined Strategy of Hybrid Zero Dynamics Feedback Control and Periodic Reward
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: In this study, we introduce an innovative gait learning methodology for three-dimensional bipedal robots, integrating Hybrid Zero Dynamics (HZD) priors with periodic reward functions to enhance gait stability, symmetry, and smooth action transitions. Notably, we employ a data-driven Bezier curve parameterization technique optimized through Reinforcement Learning (RL) to significantly improve learning efficiency and dynamic stability of the gait. The effectiveness of our approach is systematically validated across three key metrics: lateral deviation, training speed, and robustness in challenging environments. The results demonstrate our method's superiority in maintaining path stability, accelerating the learning process, and adapting to complex terrains over traditional gait learning approaches. This research not only advances the efficiency and stability of gait learning for three-dimensional bipedal robots but also provides valuable insights for future studies on robotic gait optimization.

articleTitle: A Human-machine Cooperative Control Framework for Intelligent Vehicle Considering Intervention Punishment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Uncertainty exists in human-computer interaction, which can cause conflicts between drivers and intelligent assisted driving system and reduce vehicle driving performance. An intelligent human-machine cooperative control framework based on dynamic intervention penalty is proposed. First, to address the uncertainties, the time-varying (TV) driver preview behavior and the tire nonlinear characteristics are considered in the vehicle system modelling; Second, to attenuate the conflicts between drivers and assistance steering actions, the human-machine intervention penalty factor (PF) is introduced into the driving authority allocation, and the fuzzy rule is established according to the dynamic driver torque and lateral deviation of actual preview point. Third, A Linear Parameter Varying (LPV) controller is developed to improve the control system robustness. Finally, MATLAB/Carsim joint simulation is used for experimental verification. The results show that the proposed human-machine cooperative control framework can effectively mitigate the human-machine conflict while guaranteeing the vehicle handling performance.

articleTitle: Distributed Reactive Power Optimization for Active Distribution Network Based on Network Partition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Active distribution networks (ADNs) serve as a linchpin in contemporary power systems, tasked with accommo-dating the rising penetration of renewable energy sources while ensuring efficient and reliable operation. This paper proposes a network partition-based framework for distributed reactive power optimization in active distribution networks, with the minimization of network losses during the operation of active distribution networks as the optimization objective. This paper constructs a distributed reactive power optimization model that includes both continuous and discrete devices, such as on-load tap changer (OLTC) and capacitor banks (CB). Moreover, a solution method based on the alternating optimization process (AOP) and alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) is introduced. Case study simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed reactive power optimization algorithm.

articleTitle: Distributed Drive Torque Vector Control Strategy for Energy Saving and Maneuver Optimization Synergy
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: This paper proposes a torque distribution control strategy to address the issue of increased energy consumption resulting from uneven workload between the left and right hub motors during torque vector control. The strategy coordinates direct yaw moment control with the demand for improved steering characteristics and adopts a hierarchical control architecture to optimize the energy efficiency of the chassis system and steering characteristics under steering working conditions. The steering motion's upper controller, which includes execution constraints, is designed using the MPC algorithm. The optimization problem is then transformed into a quadratic programming problem to be solved online. The lower controller deduces the globally optimal four-wheel torque distribution method under the constraints of the target yaw moment and the total longitudinal torque demand, following the principle of very small value. The algorithm's effectiveness is verified in the Carsim-Simulink simulation environment. The study investigates the influence of different control strategies on vehicle maneuvering stability and energy consumption of the electric drive system.

articleTitle: Coordinated Generation and Transmission Expansion Planning Method Considering Typhoons Disasters and Credibility of Wind Power Capacity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Against the backdrop of advancing energy transformation and the construction of new power systems, the proportion of wind power installed in China has increased significantly. Additionally, the frequency of typhoon disasters has risen, causing enormous economic losses to economically developed coastal areas. Therefore, it is urgently necessary to enhance the power system's resilience against typhoons. In order to improve the power system's resilience to typhoon weather conditions during the early stage of coordinated planning between power sources and networks, a coordinated planning model considering the credibility of typhoons and wind power capacity was established. Firstly, a typhoon wind field model and a line fault probability model were established, and the credibility of wind power capacity was evaluated. Then, based on typical fault scenarios and the credibility of wind power capacity, long-term planning was combined with short-term operations to establish a coordinated planning model considering typhoons and the credibility of wind power capacity. Finally, the effectiveness of the method was verified using the IEEE RTS-24 test system.

Author Keywords: Coordinated Planning of Generation and Transmission

articleTitle: Research on Power Decoupling Strategy of Virtual Synchronous Generator Based on Virtual Power
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Aiming at the power coupling problem caused by the high impedance ratio between the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) controlled distributed energy (DG) and the grid. In this paper, the power coupling mechanism is analyzed, the coupling degree relationship between power and impedance ratio and power angle is established by relative static gain coefficients, and a virtual power control technique based on virtual negative impedance is proposed, which calculates the virtual voltage using virtual impedance and feeds the obtained virtual voltage back to the power calculation part to form the virtual power to realize the power decoupling, and the virtual resistor and inductor specific solution methods are given based on the coupling degree constraints. Inductance specific solution method. Finally, the simulation model is built by using Matlab/Simulink simulation software. By comparing with the traditional virtual im-pedance technology, it is verified that the proposed virtual power control strategy has a significant effect on weakening the coupling between the active and reactive power loops.

articleTitle: Research on Vehicle Active Steering Control Based on Linear Matrix Inequalities
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Active front-wheel steering is the key technology to achieve vehicle handling stability, the quality of its capability has a direct influence on the automobile's stability. In view of the model uncertainty and external disturbance such as sensor noise existing in the steering control process, the present paper utilizes an active steering control of front wheel research grounded in linear matrix inequalities to study sensor noise and mechanical disturbance, etc., and builds a two-DOF vehicle model grounded in yaw and lateral motion. To enhance the robustness of the automobile within nonlinear area, by combining the magic tire model with a two-DOF vehicle dynamics model to describe the non-linearity of tire behavior, a strategy for active steering control utilizing robust <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}\infty$</tex> principles was established, and the active steering control strategy was optimized and solved utilizing linear matrix inequalities to ensure the vehicle's tracking precision and robust stability. Finally, a CarSim/Simulink co-simulation test was established. The designed controller's efficiency and durability have been validated through practical testing.
